# REQ-2234: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2234

#### Bug description

The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true. This has happened since version 3.1.1. It still worked in 3.1.0.

story.summary: The change edits TypeCollector's member-collection loops in four ways. A member whose key kind (int vs string) does not match the other members now hits `continue` right after MsgPack005 is reported. Adding a member to the int-key and string-key dictionaries is now guarded by `ContainsKey`, so a duplicate key no longer throws. Both edits are made in two parallel code paths, which look like the property loop and the field loop. The change also adds analyzer tests and run-time execution tests for `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]` types, and a README section on opting out of source generation.
story.why: Issue 2234 says the analyzer stops working for SuppressSourceGeneration types since 3.1.1. The diff implies the cause: duplicate or mixed keys made `Dictionary.Add` throw inside the analyzer, which silently killed its diagnostics. The diff does not show the cause directly. No code that gates on SuppressSourceGeneration was changed.
touches_beyond_requirement: README.md gains a new user-facing section listing which analyzer rules apply to suppressed types. It includes MsgPack012, which no test covers.
The same guards also change behaviour for normal (non-suppressed) `[MessagePackObject]` types, because the code path is shared.
New execution tests check run-time dynamic serialization of a suppressed type. That is run-time behaviour, not analyzer behaviour.
story.confidence_overview: Medium. The property-path changes are covered by markup tests that would fail on an analyzer exception (AD0001) or on missing MsgPack005. The field-path copies of the same guards have no duplicate-key test. Nothing in the diff shows that key collisions are the only reason the analyzer 'does not work' for suppressed types. The MsgPack004, MsgPack015 and MsgPack003 tests pass without any source change, so they are regression tests, not proof of the fix.
